narrative:
The model estimates a 52% chance that you will leave your job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. As a result, the company has decided not to offer you the promotion at this time.

The decision is driven mainly by three aspects of your profile. First, your total years of professional experience (1–5 years) was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward staying rather than leaving. Most employees the model expects to remain also fall in this early-career range, so the system sees you as someone still building long-term attachment. Second, the fact that you have not received other job offers while at the company also worked in your favor, again nudging the prediction toward retention; the majority of predicted stayers similarly report no external opportunities.

However, the third most influential factor worked against you. Your limited ability to participate in decisions, share opinions, or feel involved in the daily running of the team pushed the prediction noticeably toward leaving. This sense of difficult engagement is relatively uncommon among those the model expects to stay.

Taken together, the positive influences were not quite strong enough to overcome the negative effect of low involvement. The organization should consider giving you clearer channels to contribute ideas and decisions; you, in turn, may want to discuss concrete ways to increase your voice at work. Addressing this area could meaningfully shift your future prospects. (218 words)
